hints: Notice all four options use the same words: useful energy output, total energy input and energy wasted - focus on which two quantities define efficiency.
Recall that efficiency measures what fraction of the energy you supply becomes useful, so the useful output must be on top and the total input on the bottom.
Check that your ratio must be less than 1 for a real system where some input is always wasted, which rules out total input divided by useful output.
walkthrough: Identify the idea being tested: efficiency of a system describes how well input energy is converted to useful output energy.
State the governing definition: $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{useful energy output}}{\text{total energy input}}$, often multiplied by 100% to give a percentage.
Apply conservation of energy: $\text{total input} = \text{useful output} + \text{wasted output}$, so the useful output is always smaller than the total input.
Therefore the correct ratio must have useful output on the numerator and total input on the denominator, giving a value between 0 and 1.

options.A: This is the inverse of efficiency. Total input divided by useful output would give a value greater than 1.
options.B: Efficiency compares useful output to total input, not to wasted energy. Useful output divided by wasted energy is not the definition.
options.C: Efficiency is the fraction of input energy transferred usefully, so $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output} / \text{total input}$.
options.D: Wasted energy divided by total input is the fraction wasted, not the efficiency of useful transfer.
